answer: Proposed validators require each key to keep a separately salted 8-TiB encoding of the glacier archive for 40 epochs. A mesa root commits its blocks; independent auditors simultaneously request 64 unpredictable blocks per key within two seconds and plant a fable block to test rejection. A farm can share the source and rent disks, but every added identity still reserves another live 8 TiB plus concurrent reads: one encoded copy cannot answer distinct salts. Auditors sign receipts; validators deny that key’s epoch pay for missing, late or accepted fable proofs. This is not a MinePoA rule.
